title: The War Named After A Sailor's Ear
description:
The War of Jenkins' Ear (1739-1748) between Britain and Spain is named after Robert Jenkins, a British sea captain who claimed Spanish coast guards cut off his ear in 1731 while searching his ship for smuggled goods. In 1738 British politicians showed him off in Parliament to build support for war. The biggest battle was a failed British attack on Cartagena in 1741. When it ended in 1748, Britain had largely failed to get what it wanted. It is still commemorated every May in Savannah, Georgia.

Sources: Wikipedia, 'War of Jenkins' Ear'. The ear incident is Jenkins's own account ("allegedly"). The hook scene, map, giant wigs and the ear monument are dramatisations.
